title: devwork · handoff-<ISO>-<seq>.md — one session boundary (project_id + task_id are path-derived)

date.description: ISO; filename-ordered == chronological, so `ls | tail -1` is the latest

seq.description: Nth handoff of that date (filename order)

boundary.description: clean = nothing in flight, safe to start fresh. dirty = uncommitted work, paused operation, or contaminated environment. Evidence: 74% of handoffs carry both a mandate and a state recap, so the split is boundary state, not document type.

dirty_state.description: required when boundary=dirty. What a fresh session would otherwise destroy or re-run.

what.description: uncommitted diff, paused job, mutated env, corrected prior claim

task_id.description: folder slug; null for project-level handoff

cwd.description: absolute path the next session must start from

git_ref.description: branch@sha at the boundary; empty = session did not ship

reads.description: ordered absolute paths the next session loads. YAML sequences are ordered by definition, so no rank field. Most consistent component in the corpus: 45 of 60 sampled prompts.

verify.description: legitimacy smoke. A handoff that claims done is verified before anything is built on it.

expect.description: exact expected output, not a description of it

prohibitions.description: targeted imperatives ('do not relaunch the loop'). Never a catalogue of non-goals — naming what you will not do supplies vocabulary to hallucinate with.

replaces.description: DCMI dcterms:replaces — path of the handoff this one supersedes

isReplacedBy.description: DCMI dcterms:isReplacedBy — set when a later handoff supersedes this one
